core_insight: Ports & adapters isolate stable business logic from volatile infrastructure by inverting dependencies so the core defines the contract and adapters implement it.

scenes.voice: Your domain logic starts clean. Then it needs Postgres, HTTP, Kafka, Stripe. Why does it get messy so fast?
scenes.visual: Clean domain box gets tangled with DB, HTTP, Stripe icons.

scenes.voice: The real problem isn't testability. It's independence of rate of change. Business rules change slowly. Infrastructure changes fast.
scenes.visual: Two timelines: slow business rules vs fast infra changes.

scenes.voice: Obvious fix is layers. But layers still couple to specific tech through implicit contracts. Swap DB and you touch core.
scenes.visual: Layered cake with arrows leaking down to core.

scenes.voice: Ports & adapters makes the contract explicit and owned by core. Think of the app as an island. Core inside, ports are sockets on the shore, adapters are docks.
scenes.visual: Island diagram with core, ports, adapters connecting outward.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Core
        D[Domain / Use Cases]
        P[Ports - interfaces]
    end
    D --> P
    P --> A1[HTTP Adapter]
    P --> A2[DB Adapter]
    P --> A3[Payment Adapter]
    A1 -.-> Ext1[Clients]
    A2 -.-.-> Ext2[(Postgres)]
    A3 -.-.-> Ext3[Stripe/Adyen]

scenes.voice: Core defines a port like PaymentPort.charge. Adapters implement it: StripeAdapter, AdyenAdapter. Use case only knows the port.
scenes.visual: Code snippet showing interface PaymentPort and two adapters.

scenes.voice: What we gain is isolation. We can test business logic with a fake port, swap Stripe for Adyen, or move from REST to gRPC without touching core.
scenes.visual: Swap adapters under core, core stays unchanged.

scenes.voice: What we pay is indirection. Interfaces and adapters for things you may never swap. And leaky ports if you design the interface from Stripe instead of domain language.
scenes.visual: Warning icons for indirection tax and leaky port example chargeWithStripeId.

scenes.voice: Use it when future change cost exceeds indirection cost today. For a throwaway script, don't. For a core service that lives years, do.
scenes.visual: Decision scale: change cost vs indirection cost.

mental_model: Treat the application as an island. Core is the island, ports are the sockets on the shore, adapters are the docks. Dependencies always point inward, so the core stays stable while edges can be rewired.
final_takeaway: Isolate stable business logic from volatile infrastructure by letting the core define ports and adapters implement them.
